title: Tensor nonvanishing for bounded-above coherent complexes over a local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal. Work in the ordinary module derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], equipped with its canonical derived monoidal structure. Write $D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ for objects with cohomology bounded above and finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] in every degree. For $U,V\in D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ let $U\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}V$ be the derived tensor product, computed by taking bounded-above free resolutions and totalizing their tensor complex with direct sums and the differential $d(u\otimes v)=du\otimes v+(-1)^{\deg u}u\otimes dv$. Then $U\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}V\in D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$, and $U\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}V=0$ if and only if $U=0$ or $V=0$. No finite Tor-dimension hypothesis is imposed on either factor.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent, for closure under tensor; the nonvanishing assertion is an agent corollary from top cohomology of bounded-above free resolutions and Nakayama, proved in report.md.

proof.text: If $U=0$ or $V=0$, functoriality of the derived tensor and the zero object give $U\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}V=0$. For the converse assume $U$ and $V$ are both nonzero.

source.place: Derived tensor definition and zero-object property; Tag 0DJE conventions

proof.text: By the Noetherian pseudo-coherence criterion [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion], the bounded-above finitely generated cohomology hypotheses make both $U$ and $V$ pseudo-coherent. The general tensor-closure lemma [lem-trf-pseudocoherent-tensor-closure], applied with upper bounds for $U$ and $V$, shows that $U\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}V$ is pseudo-coherent; applying the same Noetherian criterion to this tensor gives the asserted bounded-above finitely generated cohomology.

Choose bounded-above finite free representatives of $U$ and $V$ from pseudo-coherence. Modify each representative at its highest nonzero term as follows. If the top cohomology vanishes, the outgoing differential is zero and the preceding differential onto the top finite free module is split surjective; its kernel is a finite projective module, hence finite free over the local ring by [lem-trf-projective-over-local-free]. Cancel the resulting contractible free summand. Repeating finitely many times reaches the highest nonzero cohomological degrees $a$ and $b$, giving bounded-above finite free complexes $P^\bullet,Q^\bullet$ with $P^i=0$ for $i>a$, $Q^j=0$ for $j>b$, and nonzero finitely generated modules $H^a(P^\bullet)\cong H^a(U)$ and $H^b(Q^\bullet)\cong H^b(V)$.

source.place: Tag 0593 (projective modules over local rings are free), together with the bounded-above finite-free definition of pseudo-coherence

proof.text: Every term of $P^\bullet$ and $Q^\bullet$ is flat, so the bounded-above flat K-flat lemma [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] identifies the derived tensor with the ordinary direct-sum total complex $T^\bullet=\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_RQ^\bullet)$, with the stated Koszul differential.

source.place: Tag 064K, bounded-above flat complexes compute derived tensor

proof.text: Apply the top-degree tensor calculation [lem-trf-local-top-degree-tensor] to $P^\bullet,Q^\bullet$. It gives $H^{a+b}(T^\bullet)\cong H^a(P^\bullet)\otimes_RH^b(Q^\bullet)$. The two factors are nonzero finite modules over the local ring, so [lem-trf-local-finite-module-tensor-nonzero] makes this cohomology module nonzero. Hence $U\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}V$ is nonzero.

source.place: Agent top-degree calculation, with Nakayama (Tag 00DV) for the finite-module tensor factor

proof.text: Thus, when both factors are nonzero, the derived tensor is nonzero; combined with Step 1 this proves $U\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}V=0$ if and only if $U=0$ or $V=0$.

source.place: Logical combination of the preceding implications
